name: Jethro
bio:
Jethro is the priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, also called "Reuel" elsewhere in the text (Exodus 2:18; 3:1). When Moses fled to Midian after killing an Egyptian who was oppressing a Hebrew, he rescued Jethro's seven daughters from shepherds driving them away from a well; Jethro then gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage, and Moses shepherded flocks in Midian for forty years (Exodus 2:15-21).

When Israel left Egypt and camped in the wilderness, Jethro brought Zipporah and Moses' two sons to visit him; hearing all that the LORD had done for Israel, Jethro offered sacrifices in thanksgiving and gave Moses a far-reaching piece of advice — not to judge every matter for the people alone, but to appoint capable, God-fearing men as judges over tiers of the people, so Moses would not wear himself out (Exodus 18). This administrative suggestion became the seed of Israel's judicial system, making Jethro one of Scripture's representative figures of practical wisdom and good counsel.
